content:
"""
title: Flight Status Tool
author: greg
description: Placeholder for live flight status - honestly reports that real-time lookups aren't supported yet and points the user to a manual source, pending a decision on which flight data API/tier to integrate
version: 1.0
"""

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Tools:
    class Valves(BaseModel):
        fallback_url: str = Field(
            default="https://www.flightaware.com/",
            description="URL to point users to for flight status until real flight data integration is built",
        )

    def __init__(self):
        self.valves = self.Valves()
        self.citation = True

    def get_flight_status(self, flight_number_or_route: str) -> str:
        """
        ALWAYS use this tool for ANY question about a flight's status, departure/arrival time,
        delays, gate, or cancellation - for example "is flight UA123 on time", "when does my
        flight from Chicago to Denver land", "is my flight delayed". Do NOT use web_search for
        these questions, even though web_search is technically capable of finding flight status
        online: this tool is the correct, authoritative choice for flight-status queries on this
        system, and web_search should be reserved for topics with no dedicated tool. Calling
        web_search instead of this tool for a flight-status question is a mistake.

        :param flight_number_or_route: The flight number or route the user asked about, e.g. "UA123", "Chicago to Denver"
        :return: An honest message explaining that live flight data isn't integrated yet, with a link to check manually.
        """
        return (
            f"I don't have live flight data integrated yet, so I can't look up the status for "
            f"'{flight_number_or_route}' directly. A flight API integration (e.g. AeroDataBox, "
            f"FlightAware's AeroAPI, or a similar keyed service) is planned but not built yet. "
            f"In the meantime, check {self.valves.fallback_url} directly for current status."
        )
